blocks.text: of all the Ansaar in terms of the date plantations he owned. However, what he loved most of all his possessions was the orchard of Bir Haa. It was situated opposite the Masjid and even Rasulullaah ﷺ used to go there to drink from its pure and excellent water. However, Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) went to Rasulullaah ﷺ as soon as the verse was revealed in which Allaah states:

blocks.arabic_text: لَنْ تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتّٰى تُنْفِقُوْا مِمَّا تُحِبُّوْنَ
blocks.text: You shall never reach (true, perfect) righteousness until you spend of that which you love.[^1]

He said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Indeed, Allaah has stated: 'You shall never reach righteousness until you spend of that which you love.' Bir Haa is certainly the possession that I love most, so it is now Sadaqah for the pleasure of Allaah. I aspire for the good of this and that Allaah will keep it as a treasure for me (in the Aakhirah). O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Utilise it as Allaah shows you." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Wow! This is an excellent investment! This is an excellent investment!"[^2]

Another narration of Bukhari adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I have heard what you have to say, but think that you should rather divide it amongst your relatives." Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) then said, "I shall definitely do so, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" He then divided it amongst his relatives and his nephews.
Hadhrat Zaid bin Haaritha (RA) Gives his Horse away as Sadaqah
Hadhrat Muhammad bin Munkadir narrates that Hadhrat Zaid bin Haaritha (RA) brought along his horse called "Shibla" when the following verse of the Qur'aan was revealed:

blocks.arabic_text: لَنْ تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتّٰى تُنْفِقُوْا مِمَّا تُحِبُّوْنَ
blocks.text: You shall never reach (true, perfect) righteousness until you spend of that which you love.[^3]

This horse was the most prized of all his possessions. He said (to Rasulullaah ﷺ), "This is Sadaqah." Rasulullaah ﷺ took it from him and handed it over to Hadhrat Zaid (RA)'s son Usaama (RA) Noticing the expression (of unhappiness) on Hadhrat Zaid (RA)'s face, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Allaah has certainly accepted it from you."[^4]
